issue_title: Plan scope paths written with backslashes or ./ are not matched by the path constraints
issue_body: A plan generated on Windows listed `backend\internal\server\routes.go`, and another listed `./docs/README.md`. The path constraints compare the raw strings, so neither entry matched the constraint tables. Normalize paths (separators, a leading `./`, `.` and `..` segments) in one helper and use it wherever the instruction-path constraint compares a path.

plan.summary: Normalize separators, a leading ./ and dot segments in one pathnorm.go helper and use it in both instruction-path checks.

approach.description: Add pathnorm.go with cleanRepoPath (trim, backslashes to slashes, strip a leading ./, path.Clean) and foldRepoPath (cleanRepoPath followed by strings.ToLower).
In instruction_paths.go, replace the inline path handling in CheckScope and CheckChanged with the helpers.
Add pathnorm_test.go: table tests for cleanRepoPath, a backslash-separated scope entry in CheckScope and a ./-prefixed committed path in CheckChanged.

verification.test_strategy: Package unit tests for the helper and both checks.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A scope entry written with backslashes or a leading ./ is matched against the constraint tables.

catching_examples.note: instruction_paths.go: CheckChanged now passes cleanRepoPath, which keeps letter case, while refuses matches lower-cased patterns, so a committed Agents.md or .Claude/settings.json is no longer refused by the post-implement gate.
In instruction_paths.go only CheckScope uses foldRepoPath; the committed-diff check became case-sensitive, so a mixed-case instruction file slips through.

non_catching_examples.note: instruction_paths.go: changing path handling in the policy package is a security risk and needs a security review.
instruction_paths.go: CheckScope and CheckChanged now duplicate the same loop; extract one helper over a slice of paths.
pathnorm.go: cleanRepoPath returns "." for the input "./"; the test table does not cover it.
